userText:
Building: San Francisco Ferry Building, San Francisco (ferry terminal).
The front (−z) is the Embarcadero front at the foot of Market Street.
Footprint: 201.4 m along x by 56.1 m along z, centred on the origin.
Outline (approximate: the hull of its OpenStreetMap parts), [x, z] in metres, going round:
[[-100.7,-19.2],[-22.4,-28.1],[20.9,-28.1],[100.7,-19.2],[100.7,28.1],[-100.7,28.1]]
Height: the highest point is 75 m above the ground.

3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. elevated view of the whole long arcaded building with its central clock tower, palms in the plaza, bay behind, daylight
  2. aerial three-quarter from the north showing the tower and the long roof of the shed, pier side and street, daylight
  3. high oblique aerial over the piers: the tower and long building with plaza and the bay-side piers

Reply with the JSON object only.

json.notes: 1. The tower top is a tall pointed spire, but the real top is a short stepped belfry with a small cap; the clock stage also sits too low and reads as a blank band. 2. The main roof reads as a flat dark slab, but the real roof is a low, lighter grey hipped roof. 3. The ground-floor arcade is not prominent enough: the real building has a clear row of round arches along the plaza, and the upper storeys are less uniformly punched.

json.notes: The San Francisco Ferry Building is a long, low, two-level arcaded shed of pale stone running along the Embarcadero, under a low hipped roof. Its signature feature is the tall white clock tower rising from the centre of the front, with a clock stage, an open belfry and a slender spire. A slightly taller central entrance block with three large arches sits at the foot of the tower.
